entries.body:
The astrology-based Lucky Star Currency project rug-pulled for $1.1 million in October 2023. You'd think that might be the end of it, but on March 22, 2024, ownership of the project was transferred to a malicious smart contract that then drained tokens priced at almost $300,000 from those who still held them.

You almost have to admire the tenacity.
entries.title: Previously rug-pulled Lucky Star Currency project somehow rugs again

entries.body:
Super Sushi Samurai, a new blockchain game on the Blast layer-2 blockchain was exploited for $4.6 million when an attacker discovered a vulnerability in its . A bug in the functionality caused users who transferred their $SSS balance to themselves to receive twice as many tokens. An attacker took advantage of this to drain $4.6 million from the project, causing the $SSS token to plummet by 99%.

The attacker contacted the project shortly after the theft, claiming to be a whitehat. They wrote, "Hi team, this is a whitehat rescue hack. Let's work on reimbursing the users." Super Sushi Samurai later confirmed that the funds had been returned, minus a 5% "bounty". The team also gave the whitehat an additional 2.5% in SSS tokens and land, and brought them on to the project team as a tech adviser.
entries.title: Super Sushi Samurai exploited by whitehat for $4.6 million

entries.body:
An attacker used social engineering techniques to gain access to the AirDAO project's liquidity pool. They then were able to drain 126.5 ETH (~$551,540) and 41.6 million AMB (notionally priced at around $500,000, but not very liquid). The thief then transferred the stolen tokens through various exchanges.

AirDAO announced the theft the following day, and stated that they were working to track and freeze stolen funds. They also offered the attacker a 10% "" if they chose to return the stolen assets.
entries.title: AirDAO exploited via social engineering attack

links.archiveTweetAlt:
Yesterday morning, a hacker drained the AMB/ETH liquidity pool after obtaining access to the LP using a social engineering scam. The scam involved an email with malicious attachments pretending to be one of our known partners.

The AMB/ETH liquidity pool contained:

35,235,955.153524583073691567 AMB
125.517550394263263045 ETH

The wallet also held ~6m AMB and some ETH for gas fees.

Altogether, the hacker took 41,612,782.10627101 AMB and 126.5 ETH.

Important reminders:

Community funds are safe.
This isolated hack only affected the wallet holding the AMB/ETH liquidity pool created by AirDAO. AirDAO community funds are safe. The AirDAO blockchain and all community members’ AMB held in exchanges are unaffected.

AirDAO Treasury funds are safe.
We hold the AirDAO Treasury in a multisignature wallet that requires seven-of-nine signatures before it makes a transaction.

Actions taken
Exchanges are working with us to track and freeze the stolen funds and have been highly responsive and cooperative.

We’re also working with Chainalysis to track the stolen funds. Following this event, we’ll strengthen our security measures and implement their Crypto Incident Response plan. We’ll also conduct our routine, company-wide review of security practices and do an additional full security audit.

We’ve also contacted other third parties, such as investors, our lawyers, specialist fraud investigators, and other security professionals.

AirDAO thanks everyone who has helped so far in tracking the funds. We’re writing a comprehensive blog post detailing every step. 

If the hacker returns the funds immediately, we'll pay a 10% white hat hacking fee. If the hacker fails to cooperate, we'll continue with law enforcement.

entries.body:
The Dolomite DEX suffered a $1.8 million theft as an exploiter was able to take advantage of a vulnerability in a that had been deployed in 2019. Although most contemporary users of the exchange use a version deployed on the Arbitrum network, the old contracts were still usable on Ethereum.

An attacker apparently discovered a reentrancy bug allowing them to drain user funds from those who had approved the old contract. Altogether, around $1.8 million was taken before the team disabled the contract. The attacker quickly the stolen funds through Tornado Cash.
entries.title: Dolomite exchange exploited for $1.8 million

entries.title: Wilder World game suffers $1.8 million theft, blames contractor
entries.body:
Wilder World is a blockchain-based racing game that uses all the buzzwords: blockchains, artificial intelligence, and . On March 16, someone with access to the project upgraded legacy contracts and transfer the project's $WILD and $MEOW tokens to themselves. Altogether, the attacker profited 515 ETH (~$1.8 million), which they then laundered through the Tornado Cash cryptocurrency .

The project blamed the theft on a previous contractor who had the private key. They also explained that the attacker seemed to be a developer based on the fact that they had "specialized knowledge of ZERO's internal security systems".

entries.body:
Someone impersonating Ansem, an influential crypto trader, was able to scam people out of more than $2.6 million simply by replying to the real Ansem's tweets. Using an account mimicking the real account, with only a slight difference in the username, a phisher convinced Ansem's followers that he was creating his own Solana and asked them to buy in.

In one of the real Ansem's tweets, Ansem wrote "i dont launch coins bros" — nevertheless, followers eager to get in early on a new memecoin clicked a link offering a presale and had their wallets .

Altogether, people lost $2.6 million to the scam. One individual lost $1.2 million.

entries.shortTitle: Remilia Collective reports multi-million dollar hack
entries.body:
"Charlotte Fang", the leader of the controversial Remilia project (known for its Milady NFTs), claimed he was hacked and drained of ETH and NFTs potentially worth several million dollars. Although the project's treasury used a model, the were stored in one password manager, which Fang says was compromised.

The attacker stole around 490 ETH (~$1.8 million) and $58,000 USDC, along with more than 130 Milady NFTs, 320 Remilio NFTs, and hundreds of derivative tokens issued on the NFTX platform. Based on , the assets are valued at north of $6 million.

The mechanism of the attack is still uncertain, though Fang has said he suspects malware that could have intercepted credentials to his Bitwarden password manager. Some have expressed skepticism around the "hack", suggesting it could have been inside job. The Remilia group had suffered a separate $1 million loss in September 2023 — blamed on a rogue developer — and failed to implement many security safeguards after that incident.
entries.title: Remilia Collective reports multi-million dollar hack

links.archiveTweetAlt:
Remilia treasury appears to have been drained

Assets from multiple official Remilia wallets have been moved to the address below and are being sold off

0x778Be423ef77A20A4493f846BdbcDDfc30252cE9 
Tweeted at 3:46 PM · Mar 16, 2024

3/16 Hack - Technical Post-Mortem

Today Remilia’s hot wallets and its multisignature treasury (https://etherscan.io/address/0xcf3e932f72e5f15411d125ad80579a3ef205b9b4…) were drained. The attack took place in two waves.

The first wave begins at 6:36pm UTC. The attacker 0x778Be423ef77A20A4493f846BdbcDDfc30252cE9 (https://etherscan.io/address/0x778Be423ef77A20A4493f846BdbcDDfc30252cE9…) begins (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x275bc80a66c8e84756d7b36e3fd5f199fe9e586848687fd62d37f5ecb321bc50…) transferring assets away from Remilia. Remilia becomes aware of the attack at approximately 7:30pm UTC.

At this point the Remilia multisignature treasury requires 3/4 signers to execute a transaction. The attacker has obtained the private keys for
- charlemagnefang.eth (https://etherscan.io/address/0x3fad44f892b986263ac69db971db8da172185387…),
- remiliadao.eth (https://etherscan.io/address/0x4Cc17f677c1271bAba0d10df83438821B5F8EAf4…),
- the first multisignature participant remiliacollective.eth (https://etherscan.io/address/0xB520F068a908A1782a543aAcC3847ADB77A04778…),
- the second multisignature participant 0x70b8fee0975b4f6249e44523df2dde3866251b96 (https://etherscan.io/address/0x70b8fee0975b4f6249e44523df2dde3866251b96…),
- the third multisignature participant 0xa77Eb0d4e2736c1FF7387CAdD3D0E6a67261a26a (https://etherscan.io/address/0xa77eb0d4e2736c1ff7387cadd3d0e6a67261a26a…),
- the Fumo ERC-20 token liquidiiy manager 0xA1A58311407Ab018141532e8Cf0a9CCCD1Bc9052 (https://etherscan.io/address/0xa1a58311407ab018141532e8cf0a9cccd1bc9052…).

The attacker transfers
- 195.1 Ether obtained from pulling liquidity from the Fumo ERC-20 token (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x394a9b1e0a397b327431eed3690301adf1483d03d0b4afd71035b9bedec44673…).
- 61 Ether from the Remilia treasury (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x21a912ae69d79e25458d7ca2ceb5cd35f85b245b55c5f510422e0807814cc5e4…).
- 110 Miladys from the Remilia treasury (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x4af80b61f19746335e80527a4a08e409e5e6d92dac371ff9448810189311078f…).
- $58k USDC from a hot wallet (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x542e7cfd3eb9776e24fc94233186571398f08f793dac8a4b194d16a6f8070caf…),
- 144 Milady from NFTx liquidity (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x879925e9321c820fc66edcb3fe4c5602e6d8c71efd50526d7cbfee77cc39dddf…),
- 105 Remilio from NFTx liquidity (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x53f1dafebf9c69877a4a2d851b88b872bf38af9d9a06c0c7411a272db7a76a9b…),
- 6 Ether and 148 Kagami from NFTx liquidity (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x875f9a126bb12085e96b7bab666e4f9a21366d6f4376fab7ce52397ada507867…).

At this point Remilia considers the feasibility of imploring NFTx to use their upgradeable contracts to rescue the NFTx tokens. Given that the contract is upgradeable (https://etherscan.io/address/0x227c7df69d3ed1ae7574a1a7685fded90292eb48#readProxyContract…), it would be possible for NFTx to have upgraded the implementation to freeze and return the attacker’s tokens, for instance. However, this rescue option remains purely an academic exercise to consider. There simply is not the time to have coordinated the upgrade in the middle of the attack.

At 8:46pm UTC, Remilia attempts to halt the attack on the Remilia multisig by increasing the signature threshold to 4/4 (https://etherscan.io/tx/0xcfadb5d2a85bf2c00d625782bfd56d18bc86641ec44f57cf97a8cf37dac7310a…). At this time it is not clear if the attacker has the private key for the fourth multisignature participant, 0x1149124FFED5Ce739bcA9dbD52348723332b4254 (https://etherscan.io/address/0x1149124FFED5Ce739bcA9dbD52348723332b4254…). After the threshold on the treasury is increased, Remilia attempts to rotate the treasury to all new multisignature participants. Out of caution and under the assumption of a browser exploit, Remilia shuts down the machines that held the hot wallets and moves to fresh hardware. After reboot, Remilia is unable to log into the Bitwarden account where the private keys and wallet passwords were stored.

The worst has happened. At this point it is clear the attacker had compromised the Bitwarden account, and now has direct access to Remilia’s private keys while Remilia no longer has been locked out of its own accounts.

Unfortunately the treasury was not secure as the private key for 0x1149124FFED5Ce739bcA9dbD52348723332b4254 was also stored in the same Bitwarden account with minor obfuscation. At 11:56pm UTC, the attacker adds himself to the multisignature treasury (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x4e1fb20d916bd32d95b43cfe2bc1ac244391ff3c685671a97666e3e93ba2777a…), proceeds to remove the other multisignature participants, and begins transferring more assets. At this point it is game over and the multisig assets are fully-compromised.

The attacker transfers
- 17.4 WETH from the Remilia treasury (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x58c4db88f0ec455dd9423bada7d5a09699a365fee42c039927018e553eba0413…),
- 3 Ether to a new wallet 0x8AC9dbd9C719806F0a48D7bC60D005AD0B18d35c (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x3e6ce0cc52c6a7fbbbf2153a9006cd3224988a783fe61a962e299c7dce001dcf…).
- 22 Miladys, 12 Bitch tees, 106 Remilios to 0x8AC9dbd9C719806F0a48D7bC60D005AD0B18d35c (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x681f09559910a8dfb0a6a02199d63d883c58b2d80a1cc7d4b95b7faad843a075…).
- 214 Remilios to 0x8AC9dbd9C719806F0a48D7bC60D005AD0B18d35c (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x3c19c315bd9750e7afaad08fa4d7dcbcf770fc1f491b972996ead00dc1065a9f…).
- 211 Ether from the Blur pool (https://etherscan.io/tx/0x94e8e2c3931250646ef017816f916b51bd6a6f03eb8aa932e3c635f217946455…).

As of writing, the attacker seems to have concluded selling every transferred NFT. Most worthwhile on-chain assets in the Remilia treasury and hot wallets have been transferred away, and as of now all the Milady and Remilio NFTs have sold been sold into bids on the market. Remilia’s primary operating treasury remains secure as it is held off-chain.

Questions:
How did the hack happen?
- Remilia doesn’t know for certain. The assumption is malware on a device that granted the attacker access to the critical Bitwarden account, or the account’s master password was brute-force cracked directly.

Why wasn’t the Fumo ERC-20 liquidity locked?
- Fumo launched as a direct Unisocks copy as a fun model for the gamified distribution of a large doll during a limited redemption period. The intention wasn’t to make a memecoin, but after launch, it was decided to allow the LP to continue beyond the closure of the redemption window to allow continued trading on the conversion to the NFT. The Fumo liquidity tokens should have been programmed to be locked, burnt, or otherwise secured after the decision was made to extend the LP indefinitely. Over-reliance on the security of the single EOA was not sufficient.

Why were all multisignature keys stored in the same Bitwarden account? Why was there no physical backup of keys? Why was there no timelock on the treasury?
- This management setup was clearly insecure. A sophisticated framework for on-chain security had been recommended shortly after the events of 9/11 but implementation was unfortunately delayed in pursuit of other priorities and left in an insecure state. Remilia is immediately moving to a correct multisignature implementation. Signers will be multiple discrete personnel using unique hardware devices instead of cloud-stored private keys prone to lockout and attacker access. Assets will be split across in multiple vaults arranged in a circle (vault one drains to vault two, vault two drains to vault three, vault three drains to vault one) with emergency fallback to different evacuation addresses. Assets will need to pass through a timelock before being transferred anywhere. Allowances will be implemented on the vaults at the contract level. In short, Remilia will be using the model seen in the battletested AssetVault system deployed here (https://etherscan.io/address/0xa74eBcBBBbA1122d57176eF5AD5b6466D60D2B33#code…). Remilia will ensure this framework is in place and transparently outlined as an immediate next steps before any new on-chain launches take place.

How does this affect Remilia NFTs?
- The contract ownership and control of the metadata for all Remilia’s NFTs had previously been migrated to the secure hardware wallet (0x54F8E4E9842c93EF0E8F5A83374db0C521D728cB), so luckily they are perfectly safe. The only major effect is the sudden supply shock of assets being dumped on the open market, which has now concluded. On the optimistic side, one can say the NFT treasury has been decentralized. Unfortunately, ownership of the $FUMO LP is compromised and not salvageable.

Will Remilia survive?
- Of course. Remilia’s primary operating treasury is held securely off-chain, leaving the runway already budgeted to pursue its planned projects unaffected, so there is no reason to not see things progress as normal. This event hurt the Fumo project and its $FUMO holders, and the price of our primary NFTs, but otherwise represented the theft of a long-term treasury of own assets which we did not have any intention to sell or liquidate any time soon. Our actual operating budget is unaffected beyond the ETH that was being held for on-chain expenses.

There is no drainer, we’re sorry but we love you. 
Tweeted at 19h

My system was hacked and it compromised all imported wallets. If you receive an odd message from any of my accounts, treat with caution. Still assessing, technical post-mortem will follow, but primary damage was the Fumo LP and the NFTs we held staked in NFTX, however NFT contract ownerships remain secure on hardware wallets. 

It appears they've already finished dumping nearly all the NFTs into bids.

I'm sorry but I love you. 
Tweeted at 21h

entries.body:
A Binance-incubated platform called NFPrompt claims to be "the first Prompt Artist Platform in Web3" — with "prompt artist" referring to people who come up with prompts to feed into large language models. More succinctly, it's a platform to sell the NFTs you've made out of AI-generated images.

The platform announced on March 15 that it had suffered a "critical security incident" that it attributed to "a group of hackers" who were able to gain access to funds belonging both to the project's users and the project itself. They did not disclose how much was taken.

The project announced that it was working with the FBI, and had contacted centralized exchanges to ask them to freeze stolen funds.
entries.title: NFPrompt discloses hack

entries.body:
The "AI-optimized" defi project Mozaic Fi was exploited by an attacker who drained around $2 million in funds from the project.

According to MozaicFi, the theft had been perpetrated by a rogue developer who was able to gain access to a private key held by a core team member. They also claimed that a simultaneous large sale of the Mozaic token resulted in cascading liquidations.

In good news for the project, the attacker moved around 90% of the stolen funds to MEXC, a centralized cryptocurrency exchange that was able to freeze the thief's access to the funds.
entries.title: Mozaic exploited for $2 million, recovers 90%

links.archiveTweetAlt:
#CertiKSkynetAlert 
@Mozaic_Fi
 has experienced an exploit with at least ~$2m lost.

Vaults belonging to the Mozaic project have been drained

Stolen funds have been transferred to Mexc 
Tweeted at 7:17 AM · Mar 15, 2024

MOZAIC SECURITY INCIDENT

What Happened
• About 12 hours ago, ~$2M in funds from the Mozaic vaults were drained by a malicious actor
• This individual was a Mozaic developer who had illegally obtained the private keys of a security module by compromising the data of a core team member
• This security module was intended as a fail-safe vault mechanism prior to the 
@HypernativeLabs
 security measures and was in the process of being phased out. This developer was aware of our recent security upgrades and took advantage of the limited window that remained. 

At the same time, an institutional investor who held a large position decided to exit their MOZ position due to the falling MOZ price/drained TVL. This large sell unfortunately led to cascading sells which resulted in a significant drop in the price of $MOZ. 
• We are in communication with this fund and maintain cordial and professional relations  

Our Response
• We were notified about this exploit by Hypernative and several other security firms
• However, by the time the vault contracts were paused, the funds had already been drained 
• Together with our security partners, we contacted the exchanges that the funds were traced to (
@MEXC_Official
 and 
@binance
), as well as the relevant law enforcement agencies 
• 90%+ of the stolen funds were sent to MEXC and frozen 
• We acknowledge that our delay in communicating this incident caused significant distress in the community. However, we were advised to avoid any public statements that may alarm the malicious actor to cause further damage to internal systems. 

What Happens Now
• We are currently sorting out the paperwork to recover the stolen funds on MEXC
• Funds sent to Binance were withdrawn on-chain and will require additional time to trace and recover
• The malicious actor has since been terminated and legal and criminal charges are being pursued against them. Additional investigations into suspected accomplices are being conducted by our security partners and law enforcement
• All Mozaic employees have had their access to internal systems removed until we complete our internal investigation
• We will also be conducting a thorough review and redesign of our security architecture to ensure that a similar incident does not occur again 

TL;DR
• This incident was the result of a malicious insider who drained the vaults
• The MOZ/xMOZ token, vault contracts, AI - remain uncompromised and secure. 
• 90%+ of stolen funds are now frozen on MEXC and will be recovered
• We are committed to making vault depositors whole, and request the patience of the community while we engage in the necessary procedures with MEXC/Binance and law enforcement. 
Tweeted at 5:40 PM · Mar 15, 2024

entries.body: The decentralized lending protocol, MOBOX, was exploited on March 14, 2024 after an attacker was able to take advantage of a bug in its referral program and borrowing functionality. By repeatedly borrowing funds and earning rewards, they were able to drain around $750,000 in USDT.
entries.title: MOBOX lending platform exploited for $750,000
